display.title: Episode 544: The Farmer Boy and the Bugle: Why We Blow the Shofar (Elul)
display.summary_short: Good, better, best in Elul; and a farmer boy learns the hard way that a fire bugle is only an alarm, just as the shofar calls us to act.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in Elul 5752. Uncle Yossi teaches the jingle 'Good, better, best, don't sit down to rest' and explains that in Elul, when we ask Hashem for the best year, we should offer Him our best: teshuvah, careful davening and brachos, and extra tzedakah, showing mercy to others as we ask Hashem for mercy. After the march, a six-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time explains the shofar of Rosh Hashanah: the Rambam says its sound is an alarm that wakes us up. A village keeps burning down, so it sends a farmer boy to the big city to learn what people do about fires. The fire chief shows him how he climbs a tower and blows a bugle. Back home, the boy blows with all his might while a whole row of houses burns down. The chief explains that the bugle only alerts people to run for water. So too, the shofar calls us to action: teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. Uncle Yossi ends with the hope of hearing the great shofar of Moshiach, then candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: The shofar is a wake-up call to act: hearing it is not enough unless we do teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.
